title: Natural signed interchange between the two cones
statement: Let $C$ be an abelian category, $A,B:C\to\mathrm{Ab}$ additive functors and $r:A\Rightarrow B$ natural. Let $F$ be the signed fibre functor [lem-amb-signed-fibre-complex] with signed shift comparison [lem-amb-signed-fibre-shift]. For each chain map $f:I\to J$, construct an isomorphism $\Phi_f:F(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(F(f))$. It sends source coordinates $(x,y,z,w)$ in order $A(J)^n,A(I)^{n+1},B(J)^{n-1},B(I)^n$ to target order $(x,z,y,-w)$. It is natural in strictly commuting squares, preserves the cone inclusion, and satisfies $F(-p)$ followed by the signed shift comparison equals $\Phi_f$ followed by the target boundary $-p$, with the cone convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tags 014E/014F; signed two-term refinement in the proof of lem-amb-signed-fibre-triangulated.

proof.text: The images under A and B of the cone projections and inclusions form inverse direct-sum decompositions, since additive functors preserve their identity and zero equations. Compose these decompositions with the explicit signed permutation and the inverse target decomposition.

Compose the proposed chain-map equation with the two target cone projections. Use the cone differential identities d_fst and d_snd, additivity and naturality of r to prove the four equations. The constructed component inverses then give a chain isomorphism.

Check naturality and preservation of the inclusion after the same two projections. The negative cone boundary followed by the shift sign and the boundary after the permutation both give (-y,w), with equal-index transports composed canonically.
